documents.name: Bodetal: Altenbrak–Thale
documents.summary: A long granite river-canyon traverse that steadily becomes steeper, rougher and more dramatic toward Thale.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The route offers a stronger complete hiking journey than a simple Brocken ascent and is one of central Germany’s most sustained canyon-like walks.

documents.name: Dahner Felsenpfad
documents.summary: A dense red-sandstone circuit threading among towers, windows, overhangs and narrow rock corridors.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Germany’s highest-density rock-landscape day hikes outside Saxon Switzerland, with strong discovery value despite the absence of a single giant summit.

documents.name: Felsenweg 6 – Teufelsschlucht
documents.summary: A full-day sandstone route through the Teufelsschlucht fissure system, rock corridors, plateaus and quarry landscapes.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It turns one of Germany’s strangest sandstone fissures into a coherent hike and provides a distinctive geological experience with little height exposure.

documents.name: Guided Sahlenburg–Neuwerk Wadden crossing
documents.summary: A guided tidal-flat crossing from the mainland to Neuwerk, walking over exposed seabed through mud, shallow water and tidal channels.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Walking across the exposed seabed to an island is one of Germany’s most distinctive non-mountain hiking experiences and genuinely worth travelling for.

documents.name: Heideschleife Wilseder Berg via Totengrund
documents.summary: A car-free heath circuit linking Totengrund, Wilsede and Wilseder Berg; extraordinary when the heath is in strong purple bloom.
documents.whyWorthwhile: At peak bloom the scale, colour and unusual car-free cultural landscape justify a major detour; outside strong bloom it drops below S-tier.

documents.name: Höllentalklamm–Höllentalangerhütte with optional Stangensteig return
documents.summary: A wet, engineered alpine gorge that opens dramatically into the Höllental basin, with an optional high return above the gorge.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Germany’s strongest combinations of route engineering, enclosed gorge scenery and a major Alpine-basin reveal. The safer gorge out-and-back preserves most of the experience if the exposed Stangensteig is unsuitable.

documents.name: Jasmund high-cliff trail: Sassnitz–Lohme
documents.summary: A proper coastal hike through UNESCO-listed beech forest with repeated reveals of white chalk cliffs and the Baltic Sea.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It is substantially richer than visiting Königsstuhl alone and represents Germany’s strongest combination of forest and active cliff coast in one continuous hike.

documents.name: Schrammsteine via Wildschützensteig
documents.summary: A sandstone route where ladders, steep stairs and narrow passages are part of the experience, culminating in one of Saxon Switzerland’s strongest ridge viewpoints.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It beats a simple Bastei visit because the hiker physically moves through the sandstone architecture. The route is exceptionally memorable without requiring climbing equipment.

documents.name: Wimbachklamm–Wimbachgrieshütte out-and-back
documents.summary: A narrow waterfall gorge followed by the immense pale debris-stream landscape of the Wimbachgries.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The landscape transition is unusually dramatic and sustained, making this substantially more destination-worthy than a short gorge visit.

documents.name: Wutachschlucht: Wutachmühle–Schattenmühle
documents.summary: A sustained wild river-gorge traverse with kilometres of forest, rough ledges, tributary cascades and changing river scenery.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few German gorge hikes maintain such a high density of river, forest and cliff scenery over an entire half-day route.

documents.name: Bielatal rock-and-ruin circuit
documents.summary: A dense sandstone circuit combining towers and ladders with a preserved blast furnace and traces of the former Schweizermühle resort landscape.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A particularly strong discovery-value alternative to Saxon Switzerland’s famous central routes, with geology and heritage in one manageable circuit.

documents.name: Breitachklamm–Engenkopf circuit
documents.summary: A deep limestone gorge with long engineered passages close to the river, extended into a worthwhile circuit above the gorge.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The depth and sustained proximity to the torrent make this one of Germany’s strongest accessible limestone-gorge experiences.

documents.name: Darß Weststrand–Darßer Ort circuit
documents.summary: A long coastal circuit through wind-shaped Darß forest, shifting dunes and the wild Weststrand rather than a conventional Baltic promenade.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Germany’s best non-cliff coastal hikes and worth a major detour for its sustained wild-coast character.

documents.name: DonauWelle Eichfelsen-Panorama
documents.summary: A limestone-cliff circuit with repeated high viewpoints into the sharply incised Upper Danube valley.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of southern Germany’s strongest non-Alpine panorama hikes and worth a major detour in clear weather.

documents.name: EA1 Schluchtentour: Landgrafenschlucht–Drachenschlucht
documents.summary: A mossy ravine circuit whose highlight, Drachenschlucht, narrows into an almost body-width rock corridor.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The extraordinary constriction of Drachenschlucht plus a second ravine makes this one of central Germany’s most distinctive short hiking days.

documents.name: Ehrbachklamm circuit from Oppenhausen
documents.summary: A rough slate ravine hike with wet boulders, roots and assisted passages that feels unusually wild for western Germany.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Longer, rougher and more immersive than many better-known western German ravine walks, while staying below technical scrambling.

documents.name: Eistobel–Riedholzer Kugel circuit
documents.summary: A concentrated waterfall gorge of cascades, pools and rock constrictions, strengthened by continuing over the Riedholzer Kugel ridge.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It offers a better overall hike than simply walking into the gorge and back, particularly in periods of good but safe water flow.

documents.name: Feldbergsteig
documents.summary: A compact high-Black-Forest circuit mixing open Feldberg summit country, rough forest trails and glacial landforms.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major-detour hike and the strongest compact introduction to the High Black Forest for a non-technical hiker.

documents.name: Gangolfsberg basalt circuit from Oberelsbach
documents.summary: A quiet Rhön circuit through old beech forest to a striking wall of organ-pipe basalt columns.
documents.whyWorthwhile: An under-recognised geology-and-forest combination that deserves a major detour, especially in spring woodland bloom or autumn colour.

documents.name: Guided Föhr–Amrum Wadden crossing
documents.summary: A guide-only island-to-island crossing over the tidal seabed between Föhr and Amrum, including meaningful tidal-channel crossings.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Germany’s most unusual destination-worthy walking experiences, especially valuable for catalogue diversity beyond mountain hiking.

documents.name: Luisenburg Felsenlabyrinth–Kösseine circuit
documents.summary: A granite-maze circuit that threads the Luisenburg boulder labyrinth before continuing as a genuine summit hike to the Kösseine.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the strongest non-Alpine rock-labyrinth hikes in Germany and a destination-worthy Fichtel Mountains discovery.

documents.name: Lusen via Teufelsloch and Himmelsleiter
documents.localName: Über Teufelsloch und Himmelsleiter zum Lusen
documents.summary: A granite summit route that rises from forest through Teufelsloch and the long Himmelsleiter staircase onto the Lusen blockfield.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The route supplies a genuinely distinctive mountain landscape without Alpine technicality and is considerably more memorable than a generic forest summit.

documents.name: Muggendorfer Gebürg cave-and-karst circuit
documents.summary: A limestone-karst circuit where naturally passable caves, collapsed terrain and rock formations are part of the walking route itself.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A rare coherent non-technical cave-and-karst hike and one of Franconian Switzerland’s best alternatives to more climbing-oriented routes.

documents.name: Oybin–Gratzer Felsen–Töpfer–Scharfenstein circuit
documents.summary: A compact Zittau Mountains sandstone circuit linking rock ridges, isolated towers and several elevated viewpoints.
documents.whyWorthwhile: An overlooked sandstone route with major-detour value for hikers who particularly enjoy rock landscapes.

documents.name: Partnachklamm–Bockhütte–Reintal circuit
documents.summary: A substantial mountain-valley circuit that turns the famous Partnachklamm into the opening act of a full hiking day.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It preserves the gorge’s spectacle while avoiding the weakness of treating it as a short standalone tourist stop.

documents.name: Pellenzer Seepfad
documents.summary: A volcanic Eifel circuit linking crater-lake scenery, exposed ash deposits, quarry landscapes and visible mofette activity.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few German day hikes combine so many volcanic processes in one coherent route; it is one of the catalogue’s strongest geology-led discoveries.

documents.name: Rißlochfälle–Großer Arber ascent
documents.summary: A steep one-way climb past the Rißloch waterfalls to the highest summit of the Bavarian Forest.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It combines the region’s strongest waterfall landscape with a meaningful summit ascent; using the gondola and bus for the return avoids turning it into a weaker descent-heavy loop.

documents.name: Uracher Wasserfallsteig
documents.summary: A steep Swabian Jura circuit combining Urach waterfall, active tufa formation and a real escarpment ascent.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The waterfall is only one component of a compact, varied Alb day hike, giving it substantially more value than an attraction-only visit.

documents.name: Bruchhauser Steine circuit
documents.summary: A Sauerland circuit built around four enormous volcanic rock monoliths rising above upland forest.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A very good regional hike whose exceptional central formation justifies inclusion, but not usually a major trip across Germany.

documents.name: Falladas Fridolinwanderung
documents.summary: A lowland lake-and-forest circuit made memorable by a hand-operated cable ferry across a narrow glacial lake.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A strong in-region discovery rather than a Germany-wide destination hike, but valuable because it represents a genuinely distinctive lowland experience.

documents.name: HO7 Hohenstein route
documents.summary: A Weser Uplands circuit centred on the surprisingly large Hohenstein limestone cliffs above the wooded valley.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Worth doing when already in the region and useful geographic diversity, but not strong enough to justify cross-country travel by itself.

documents.name: Schlaubetal-Wanderweg: Müllrose–Wirchensee
documents.summary: A long lowland traverse through stream valleys, lakes, wetlands, ravines and historic mill landscapes in eastern Brandenburg.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of northeastern Germany’s strongest long lowland hikes, retained at B because the spectacle is diffuse rather than concentrated.
